title: upgrade-attn-kernels-flashattnv2-rope-rotary-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Upgrade attention kernels to latest FlashAttentionV2 variant with fused rotary/rope ops, fused QKV transpose + softmax kernel paths, and optimized KV-cache layout to improve throughput and tail latency for streaming and long-context workloads. This PR also adds scheduler heuristics and continuous-batching hints so runtime can maintain low p99 latency while increasing average GPU utilization. Motivation: recent customer workloads and internal perf runs show our previous attention path underutilizes tensor cores on A100/A10G for medium-seq batched workloads and pays extra overhead for rotary/rope encoding when using separate kernels. Goals: (1) Replace slow elementwise rotary application with fused rotary variants in FlashAttnV2 where available, (2) introduce a fused QKV->softmax kernel to reduce memory bandwidth and kernel-launch overhead, (3) change KV-cache layout to interleaved blocks to improve cache locality for continuous-batching, (4) add scheduler tuning knobs (max_batch_delay_ms, preferred_batch_shape) and a canary rollout for the new kernels. Compatibility & rollout: feature-flagged under "flashattn_v2_fused" and "kv_interleaved_cache". Safeguards include CPU fallback, previous kernel fallback for models with custom rotary/rope hooks, and per-model perf thresholds for automatic rollback during canary. Benchmarks: internal microbench on Llama-2-13B and RW-Redwood-7B show median throughput +18-32% and p99 latency -12-20% for common seq lengths (128/512/2048) when using fused kernels and interleaved KV cache with continuous batching enabled. On smaller models (<=3B) gains are present but smaller (~6-12%) due to memory-bound behavior. Testing: unit tests for kernel selection, integration GPU tests for correctness vs reference (float32/float16/quantized), end-to-end streaming smoke tests, and a perf harness that produced the numbers above. Checklist: - [x] Kernel upgrades and new fused kernels integrated - [x] KV-cache layout change with migration path - [x] Scheduler heuristics and config knobs documented - [x] Flag gating and canary rollout plan - [x] Benchmarks and perf harness artifacts attached - [x] Backcompat tests and CPU/fallback verified
References: Linear ENG-3421 (serve perf initiative), ENG-4120 (kv-cache work). Related PRs: pr-613579, pr-635001 (previous flashattn v2 tuning), pr-55678 (initial rope/rotary support).

b2c3d4e: add fused rotary/rope JNI wrapper + CUDA kernel selection logic
c3d4e5f: implement interleaved KV-cache layout and migration helpers
d4e5f6a: scheduler heuristics: max_batch_delay_ms and preferred_batch_shape

review_thread: Ethan Cole: Can we add a regression test that runs on CI small-GPU (T4) to validate correctness for quantized paths?
Priya Nair: Added kv_cache_migration_tests and attn_kernel_tests covering quantized int8 path; CI GPU integration also covers a minimal quantized smoke test.
Ava Martinez: The scheduling defaults look aggressive for small customers. Suggest lowering preferred_batch_shape default and exposing env var to opt-in to more aggressive packing.
Priya Nair: Agreed, lowered default preferred_batch_shape and added env var REDWOOD_BATCHER_AGGRESSIVE=true to opt in. Documented in scheduler/config.h and docs.
Liam Zhao: Observability: we need per-model counters for kernel variant chosen and fallback counts to track canary. Add metrics emit points.
Priya Nair: Added metrics: attn.kernel.variant (string) and attn.kernel.fallback_count (int) and hooked into console dashboards.
ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (bench harness recorded results; artifacts uploaded)
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 fused variants with rope/rotary fusion and interleaved KV-cache layout. Expect 18-32% throughput improvement on medium/large models and lower p99 latency for streaming workloads. Feature gated and canary rolled out. See docs/perf/attn_kernels.md for tuning knobs.
canary_rollout_plan: enable feature flag in 5% of serving clusters for 48h; monitor attn.kernel.fallback_count, p95/p99 latency, and error rates; if regressions >5% rollback automatically; expand to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with incremental thresholds
notes: This PR touches low-level GPU kernels. Ops was consulted for canary nodes. Security reviewed native bindings change due to new JNI wrapper. No user-facing API change.
